title: Aa Perm
scramble: x R2' D2' R U R' D2' R U' R x'
story:
<!-- Case: Aa-Perm -->

## Overview
Clockwise corner cycle: headlights on the left, matching colors on the front, and no edge swaps—classic Aa silhouette.

## Recognition
- Left face shows a block/headlights, while the other three corners need to cycle clockwise.
- Edges already match their centers, confirming only the corners move.
- Compared to Ab, the desired cycle direction is clockwise.

## Technique
1. Execute `x (R' U R') D2 (R U' R') D2 R2 x'`.
2. Focus on crisp `D2` turns so alignment stays perfect.
3. Track the solved block on the left; it never moves, making AUF simple.

## Fingertricks
- Treat `D2` as table turns using ring fingers to avoid regrips.
- Keep your left thumb anchored on the front-left sticker during the opening `x` rotation.

## Common Mistakes
- Mixing up the direction and accidentally running Ab.
- Letting the cube drift during `D2`, which throws off the final AUF.

## Practice
- Drill the alg slowly while verbalizing “clockwise” to lock in directionality.
- Aim for sub‑1.2s execution once the rhythm feels natural.

## Related Cases
- [Ab-Perm](deddal://case/Ab-Perm) – Counter-clockwise sibling.
- [E-Perm](deddal://case/E-Perm) – Double corner swap when headlights face each other.

## Pro Tips
- Because the solved block stays on the left, practice keeping your eyes on the unsolved corners throughout; it improves AUF accuracy.

title: Ab Perm
scramble: x R' U R' D2' R U' R' D2' R2' x'
story:
<!-- Case: Ab-Perm -->

## Overview
Counter-clockwise corner cycle with the same silhouette as Aa—headlights on the left, edges solved, but the corners rotate the opposite direction.

## Recognition
- Headlights sit on the left; the remaining corners must cycle counter-clockwise.
- Edges already match, confirming this is a corner-only PLL.
- Perfect mirror of the Aa pattern, so pay attention to the direction arrows.

## Technique
1. Run `(x) R D' R U2 R' D R U2 R2 (x')`.
2. Keep `D/D'` turns smooth so the cube alignment stays intact.
3. Watch the solved headlights; they remain on the left the whole time.

## Fingertricks
- Push `D'` with your right ring finger and pull `D` with the same finger on the return.
- Use the opening `x` rotation to get comfortable finger access to the D layer.

## Common Mistakes
- Accidentally executing the Aa algorithm (clockwise) and making the case worse.
- Sloppy `D` turns causing misalignment before AUF.

## Practice
- Drill in pairs with Aa so you can instantly feel the difference in direction.
- Aim for the same execution time as your Aa perm to keep PLL consistency.

## Related Cases
- [Aa-Perm](deddal://case/Aa-Perm) – Clockwise version.
- [E-Perm](deddal://case/E-Perm) – Another corner-only PLL but with double swaps.

## Pro Tips
- Verbally note “counter-clockwise” before executing to avoid mix-ups during speed solves.

title: E Perm
scramble: x' D R U R' D' R U' R' D R U' R' D' R U R' x y'
story:
<!-- Case: E-Perm -->

## Overview
Double diagonal corner swap: headlights face each other and every corner must move across the cube while edges stay solved.

## Recognition
- Headlights on the front and back stare at each other.
- Side faces show alternating colors with no solved blocks.
- Edges already match their centers, so only the corners are affected.

## Technique
1. Execute `(y x') (R U' R' D) (R U R' D') (R U R' D) (R U' R' D') (x)`.
2. Focus on keeping `D` turns shallow and consistent.
3. Finish by undoing the initial rotations to return to your reference orientation.

## Fingertricks
- Treat the repeated `(R U R' D)` packets as rhythmic beats; say them out loud while practicing.
- Keep the cube slightly lifted so D turns glide like table moves.

## Common Mistakes
- Miscounting the packets and ending with a half-solved pattern.
- Overshooting D turns and scrambling the cross.

## Practice
- Drill slowly to internalize the alternating `U`/`U'` pattern, then push tempo.
- Alternate with Aa/Ab perms to balance corner-only PLL coverage.

## Related Cases
- [Aa-Perm](deddal://case/Aa-Perm) and [Ab-Perm](deddal://case/Ab-Perm) – Corner-only PLLs with single 3-cycles.

## Pro Tips
- Because edges stay fixed, pre-plan AUF before the final `(x)` undo to save time.

## Overview
First N-perm—diagonal corner swap with complex edge cycling, creating distinctive asymmetric pattern.

## Recognition
- No solved pieces or headlights.
- Asymmetric pattern (not symmetrical like H or E).
- Two bars visible on adjacent sides.

## Technique
1. Position bars correctly for Na-perm.
2. Execute `R U R' U R U R' F' R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U2 R U' R'`.
3. Long algorithm with F-move integration.

## Fingertricks
- Initial R U R' U R U R' flows smoothly.
- F' transition requires index finger.
- Middle section uses familiar triggers.
- Final U2 provides transition time.

## Common Mistakes
- Confusing with Nb-perm—bar positions differ slightly.
- Getting lost in the long sequence.
- Breaking rhythm during F-move transitions.

## Practice
- Drill 20 times to fully memorize.
- Break into chunks: setup, F-section, finish.
- Practice with Nb-perm for comparison.

## Related Cases

- [V-Perm](deddal://case/V-Perm) – Diagonal corner swap.
- [Y-Perm](deddal://case/Y-Perm) – Another diagonal swap.

## Pro Tips
- N-perms are rare—don't over-practice.
- Bar positions distinguish Na from Nb.
- Some solvers use alternative algorithms.

## Overview
Anti-clockwise three-edge cycle—corners stay solved, three edges cycle counter-clockwise.

- All four corners already solved (four headlights visible).
- Three edges need cycling.
- One solved edge acts as anchor.

## Technique
1. Position solved edge on back.
2. Common algorithm: `M2 U M U2 M' U M2`.
3. M-slice moves create fast execution.

## Fingertricks
- Ring fingers drive M-slice moves.
- M2 uses quick double flick.
- U and U2 moves with index fingers.
- Very fast with good M-slice technique.

## Common Mistakes
- Weak M-slice technique—practice separately.
- Confusing with Ub-perm (opposite cycle direction).
- Not positioning solved edge correctly.

## Practice
- Drill M-slice moves in isolation first.
- Practice 20 reps for fluency.
- Compare with Ub-perm to sharpen recognition.

- [H-Perm](deddal://case/H-Perm) – Edge swaps.
- [Z-Perm](deddal://case/Z-Perm) – Adjacent edge swap.

- Very common case—execute quickly for better times.
